findings.summary: An existing test fails once the CHANGELOG holds 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', and the Dependents list leaves that test out.
findings.evidence: I read this existing test. It collapses the whole of CHANGELOG.md (line 6959-6962) and asserts `!text.contains("expected 3% of newly refused readings")` with the message "still holds the share of D164" (line 6977-6980). Step 7 and criterion 2 add exactly that sentence to the CHANGELOG. The test would then fail, so criterion 6 (cargo test passes) fails. The Dependents entry for CHANGELOG readers names only reading.rs:5224 and refusal_corpus.rs:2302-2308 and leaves this reader out. A Grep for negative `expected N%` assertions finds only this one. Fix: Add this test to the Dependents list. Narrow its negative assertion on the changelog to the defined-terms item: find the Unreleased item by its own cause text, the way reading.rs:5232-5245 does, and check only that item. The doc-comment half can stay as it is. Keep the positive assertions, and say in the test why the scope changed: another check now declares 3% (D165 history). Run `cargo test -p athena-core defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` as that dependent's test. Reading.rs is already a deliverable, so no new file is needed.
findings.location: Plan step 7 (CHANGELOG item) and the Dependents list; crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:6947-6981 `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended`

findings.summary: 'runner' and 'workflow' count as a CI place on their own, so non-CI caches can trigger D1.
findings.evidence: Athena's own wording uses 'runner' for non-CI things; the plan itself says 'the corpus runner'. 'Workflow' is also used generically. So a behavior criterion such as 'the corpus runner caches the readings' meets D1 with no CI cache involved. This is an estimate from wording; I did not count how often it occurs in stored readings. Fix: Count runner(s) or workflow(s) as a CI place only beside CI, GitHub or Actions, or only when the reading has a `.github/workflows/` deliverable. Add a 'the corpus runner caches the readings' accept control.
findings.location: Decision 6 / Step 1, ENV_CI_PLACE_WORDS (runner, runners, workflow, workflows)

findings.summary: The plan does not say which corpus case carries each of the four new INPUT_FORMS tags.
findings.evidence: `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` requires every listed tag to appear on at least one case. Step 6 maps some existing tags to cases explicitly, but does not say which cases carry the four new tags (ci-cache-criterion, ci-result-reuse-criterion, cache-scope-assumption, cache-word-in-product-or-path). Fix: Name, for each of the four new tags, the corpus case that carries it.

summary: I read the code and found no misreading of the request, but the plan needs one revision before it can pass cargo test. The design holds up: it extends check_environment_reach where the missing step starts, uses a narrowed D2 that leaves SHA-matched reuse alone, judges completeness on the best single assumption instead of the union, keeps the old message tail unchanged, and detects actions/cache with a separate token test. I checked it against surveys.rs:373-869 and the reading.rs fixtures. CI_ENVIRONMENT (reading.rs:4470) has no cache noun, so it never counts as a candidate assumption. Tracing the job's own criterion text shows the older host-action block fires on 'main branch push run', and the reading's Environment: assumption satisfies both the old block and the new one. The plan breaks one test it does not list. `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` (reading.rs:6947-6981) asserts that the whole CHANGELOG does not contain 'expected 3% of newly refused readings', which is the sentence criterion 2 requires. The plan must narrow that assertion to the defined-terms item and list the test as a dependent. Two smaller points: 'runner' and 'workflow' count as CI places on their own, which risks false positives, and the plan does not say which corpus case carries each new tag.
